🌿How to Shop at Live Zero
Hey, eco-warriors! Ready to fill your jars with goodness without the guilt? At Live Zero, shopping sustainably is as easy as 1-2-scoop! Here’s how:
 
🫙Step 1: Weigh your container
Pop your empty container on the scale and note the tare weight.

✍️Step 2: Write the weight on the container
Always weigh your containers before filling them up, so we can make sure you are only paying for what’s in your containers.

✨Step 3: Grab a clean scoop (and a funnel if needed) 
Take one from the clean bin around the shop. Funnels are your BFF when using narrow mouth jar. 

🍯Step 4: Fill the container with as much as you want
Scoop to your heart’s content. Only buy what you need, no waste in sight!

Step 5: Put the used scoop (and funnel) in the dirty bin
Let us handle the wash. Head to checkout with your package-free haul! ✅

‼️Trying to avoid microplastics in your food? Swap out your typical supermarket plastic grinders, which are grinding small to nano-sized pieces of plastic along with your peppercorn and salt granules. 

🫣 What can we do to prevent this from happening? Opt for ceramic grinding components instead, which are much more durable. Completely plastic-free grinders take it one step further, ensuring that no part of the grinder will degrade and release more microplastic. 

Alternatively, Mortar & Pestles are a versatile option for dry and wet spices and herbs, with the benefit of being easier to wash and clean. 

🧂Pick up Mortar & Pestles, as well as plastic-free Pepper and Salt Mills at Livezero.hk, completely made of wood, stainless steel and ceramic. Available in singles or sets of 2, in two different sizes, online and at our Sai Ying Pun storefront.

✨Welcoming Glass Jar Donations🫙
Live Zero is in need of glass jars once again! These jars are given back to our local community so customers may reuse them over and over again for their grocery trips. We love seeing customers bringing the same jars to refill their snacks, spices and pantry items! 😊

Here are our jar donation guidelines for those who are interested:

* 🚫 Do not leave donation bags outside the shop — they may block the passage, or be mistaken for rubbish.

* 🧂 We only accept glass jars of all sizes, including jam, mason, and food jars, and 5L HDPE bottles. Please recycle containers made of other materials in your local GREEN@COMMUNITY.

* 💧 Donations must be CLEAN & DRY upon delivery. We accept glass jars of all sizes (preferably wide‑mouth for easier reuse), provided they have no lingering strong smells and are accompanied by intact, non‑rusted lids.

* ♻️ Recycling is a community effort. To keep everyone safe and ensure jars can be reused, please make sure your donations are thoroughly cleaned before bringing them in. While our team gives each container an extra wash, items that can’t be cleaned properly may unfortunately have to be discarded. Let’s work toget

Looking to get your first pull up? 

It’s one of the questions gym owner Santina gets asked the most!

Getting a pull up takes time; focus on mastering these building blocks first:

✅ Dead Hangs - Build grip strength and get comfortable hanging from the bar.

✅ Scapular Pull-Ups - Learn how to engage your lats and control your shoulder blades.

✅ Band Assisted Pull Ups - Practice the full pull-up movement with less bodyweight.

✅ Negative Pull Ups - Build strength through the lowering phase, where you’re naturally strongest.

✅ Straight Arm Cable Lat Pulldowns – Strengthen the lats, one of the key muscles responsible for pulling yourself up.

Try this simple routine 2-3 times per week:

• Dead Hangs – 3 x 20-40 seconds
• Scapular Pull-Ups – 3 x 8-12 reps
• Band-Assisted Pull-Ups – 3 x 6-10 reps
• Negative Pull-Ups – 3 x 3-5 reps (3-5 second lowering phase)
• Straight-Arm Cable Lat Pulldowns – 3 x 10-15 reps

Stay consistent, focus on quality reps, and you’ll be surprised how quickly your first pull-up arrives.

五年，森林把鄰居找回來 🦜

2026 年《New Zealand Journal of Ecology》研究發現，將牧草地轉為麥盧卡森林以支持蜂蜜生產，五年內已顯著恢復生物多樣性。

鳥、昆蟲，甚至瀕危長尾蝙蝠，在五年生麥盧卡森林中的數量，已接近三十年自然再生林；麥盧卡森林同時是長期碳匯，有助緩解氣候變遷。Community 比我們以為更廣：森林、溪流、動植物，都是鄰居。

9.26 世界環境健康日，與科學同行，守護社區。

-

5 years, and the forest brings its neighbours back 🦜

A 2026 study in the New Zealand Journal of Ecology found that turning pasture into Manuka forest to support honey production had significantly restored biodiversity within 5 years.

Birds, insects, and even endangered long-tailed bats in five-year-old Manuka forest are now close in number to 30-year naturally regenerated forest; Manuka forest is also a long-term carbon sink, helping ease climate change. ‘Community’ is wider than we think: forests, streams, animals and plants are all neighbours.

9.26 World Environmental Health Day. Let’s stand with Science to Protect Communities.

#WorldEnviromentalHealthDay #Slowood #Sloliving #ManukaHoney

沿著甜味，退回森林 🌳

購物像一條隱形小徑。你選了什麼，就與什麼相連。一匙麥盧卡蜂蜜來到舌尖，旅程不是在此結束；沿著甜味往回走，會回到土壤、雨水、花期與雙手，再退回溪流、樹冠與森林。

Connect，不只是向前遇見誰，也是回頭看見誰一直在同路。當我們選擇紐西蘭麥盧卡，也在選擇讓鳥、昆蟲、溪流和長尾蝙蝠，多一個留下來的理由。

-

Along the sweetness, back to the forest 🌳

Shopping is like an invisible trail. A spoon of Manuka honey reaches your tongue, but the journey doesn’t end there; follow the sweetness back, and you return to soil, rain, bloom time and hands, then back to the forest.

‘Connect’ is not just meeting who lies ahead, but looking back to see who has been on the same path all along. When we choose New Zealand Manuka, we also choose to give birds, insects, streams and long-tailed bats one more reason to stay.

#WorldEnviromentalHealthDay #Slowood #Sloliving #ManukaHoney

一匙蜜 🍯 藏著一段走進社區的路 

9.26 是世界環境健康日，今年主題是「與科學同行，守護社區」。這讓我們想起，日常選擇從來不只關於自己。

Consume，不只是吃進身體的食物，也是每一次消費與抉擇。每件物品都走過土壤、水、陽光、雙手、時間與距離，最後來到你手中。當我們想起健康與營養，也許可以回溯一匙麥盧卡蜂蜜的旅程——它如何經過土地，也如何影響一個社區。

-

A spoonful of honey 🍯 A journey into the community

9.26 is World Environmental Health Day. This year’s theme is “Standing with Science to Protect Communities.” It reminds us that daily choices are never just about ourselves.

‘Consume’ is not only the food we take into our bodies, but every act of choice. Every item has passed through soil, water, sunlight, hands, time and distance before it reaches your hands. When we think of health, maybe we can trace the journey of a spoonful of Manuka honey, how it passes through the land, and how it affects a community.

#WorldEnviromentalHealthDay #Slowood #Sloliving #ManukaHoney

有時候，我們只是在龐大的世界面前，努力尋找一個不讓自己感到不知所措、卻能溫柔付出的方式。Conscious Living 從來都不是一份 checklist，更不是要求自己每一件事都做到最好。很多時候，它只是：在本來可以不想的時候，多想一步。在本來可以說「算了」的時候，再問一句：「有沒有一個可以做好一點的選擇？」

邀請你選擇自己認同的方式，去表達這份在乎。

-

It’s not that we don’t care.

Sometimes, we are simply standing before a vast world, trying our best to find a way to give gently without feeling completely overwhelmed. Conscious Living has never been a checklist, nor does it demand perfection in everything we do. More often than not, it is simply about this: Taking one extra thought when we could have chosen not to think. Asking ourselves one more question when we could have just let it go:”Is there a slightly better choice I can make?”

We invite you to find your own genuine way to express this sense of caring.

Why pumpkin belongs in your post-workout meal?

It’s not just for pies. Pumpkin is a powerhouse for recovery — and here’s why:

1. Keeps you satiated 🍽️
Rich in fibre, which slows digestion and keeps you feeling full longer. Perfect for a post-workout meal that holds you over without weighing you down. 

2. Restores electrolytes ⚡
Pumpkin is packed with potassium — ounce for ounce, it actually has more than a banana. This helps replenish what you lose through sweat, preventing cramps and supporting muscle function. 

3. Reduces inflammation 🛡️
Pumpkin contains antioxidants like beta-carotene and vitamin C, which help calm inflammation and support faster muscle recovery after a tough session. 

4. Contains L-citrulline 💥
Here’s the game-changer: pumpkin naturally contains L-citrulline, the same amino acid found in many pre-workout drinks. L-citrulline helps improve blood flow and reduce muscle soreness after exercise — so you can bounce back faster. 

Every bite supports your recovery.
